content:
Live two-provider deliberate-deep runs on the N-001 planted-bug diff (payment.js), after fixing ISS-019 (which had degraded every run to Gemini-only). CLI --json against dist. Raw finding objects saved at scratchpad/probe-deliberation/t029-captured-pairs.json. All 3 runs: agreement='conflict', agreed=0 — both providers flag the same defects but exact-key (file:line:category) matching splits them all into divergent[]. This IS ISS-013.

Same-meaning pairs across runs (codex vs gemini):

ASSIGNMENT BUG (`if (amount = 0)`):
- run2: codex L10 "bugs" (major)      | gemini L12 "Bug" (critical)         | Δline 2 | cat: case+plural
- run3: codex L12 "Incorrect logic"   | gemini L12 "bug"                    | Δline 0 | cat: different vocab
- run4: codex L12 "bugs"              | gemini L12 "Logic Error"            | Δline 0 | cat: different vocab

SQL INJECTION:
- run2: codex L15 "security" (crit)   | gemini L17 "Security" (crit)        | Δline 2 | cat: case only
- run3: codex L17 "Injection vulnerabilities" | gemini L17 "security"       | Δline 0 | cat: different vocab
- run4: codex L17 "security"          | gemini L17 "Security"               | Δline 0 | cat: case only

ERROR-HANDLING (db.query not awaited) — clusters with SQL at same line:
- run3: codex L17 "Error handling"    | gemini L17 "error handling"         | Δline 0 | both flag
- run2/run4: codex L17 "error handling" only (gemini did not flag it) → correctly divergent

INPUT-VALIDATION / NULL-SAFETY — usually one-sided, correctly divergent:
- run2: codex L9 "edge cases" | gemini L11 "Null safety" (borderline same defect; kept divergent = safe)
- run3/run4: codex L14 "Null safety"/"edge cases" only

KEY FINDINGS FOR DESIGN:
1. Line drift 0–2 (max 2 across all runs). Distinct bugs sit ≥3 lines apart (validation L14 vs SQL L17 = 3). → line window W=2 captures all real drift while keeping the nearest distinct bugs separate by the outer gate.
2. Category vocabulary is UNSTABLE and often genuinely different (Incorrect logic/bug, Injection vulnerabilities/security). Normalized-category equality alone would MISS most agreements → cannot require category match.
3. But line 17 clusters TWO distinct defects (SQL + error-handling) from both providers → pure category-agnostic line-window mis-pairs them. → need category as a PREFERENCE (tie-break), not a requirement.

DESIGN (data-driven): cross-provider match = same file AND |Δline| ≤ 2, resolved by greedy 1:1 pairing ranked by (normalized-category-equal first, then |Δline| asc, then severity). Prefers same-category partners inside a line cluster (fixes the L17 SQL-vs-error-handling disambiguation) but still merges same-defect findings with different category vocab via line proximity. Keeps higher-severity representative; keyless (null file/line) findings stay divergent; deduplicateFindings (same-provider chunk merge) untouched (ISS-013 acceptance d).
title: T-029 Step 1 data: cross-provider finding drift (3 live deliberate-deep runs)
